chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man from the clan of my uncle, and he is a man from your righteous mawla (clients/friends), has instructed me to ask you about al-nabidh, so I should describe it to you.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I shall describe it to you.'
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited; therefore, whatever its large quantity intoxicates, its small quantity is prohibited.'
I said, 'So the small quantity of the prohibited substance is made permissible if a large quantity of water is added?'
So he responded to him with his palm twice: 'No! No!'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: A specific type of fermented drink made from raisins or dates, used here as the example for intoxicants.
key_terms.صُلَحَاء: Plural of salih, meaning righteous or pious men.
key_terms.مَوَالِي: Clients or freedmen; here referring to the followers or associates of the Imams.

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on diluting an intoxicant with water?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia legal principle of 'tadarruj' (gradualism) in the prohibition of intoxicants, establishing that the quality of intoxication renders the entire substance haram regardless of quantity. Imam al-Sadiq (as) explicitly rejects the counter-argument that diluting a small amount of intoxicant with abundant water renders it permissible, a view held by some jurists who distinguished between quantity and quality. This hadith underscores the definitive nature of the Prophet's statement 'kullu muskirin haram' as the primary criterion, overriding mere volumetric changes.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man from the Clan of Umayya, and he is a man from your righteous friends, has instructed me that I should ask youasws about Al-Nabeez, so I should described it to youasws’. So heasws said: ‘Iasws shall describe it for you.
Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is prohibited, therefore whatever, if a lot of it intoxicates, so a little of it is prohibited’.
I said, ‘So the little of it is Prohibited, so would it be Permissible if most of it is the water?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> responded to it with his<sup>asws</sup> palm twice: ‘No! No!’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that a man of the virtuous ones among your followers has asked me to ask you about al-Nabidh (wine) so I can describe it for him from you.

He (the Imam) said, ‘I describe it for you as the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Every intoxicating liquor is unlawful and whatever in a large quantity is intoxicating liquor, it in a small amount is unlawful.’
I then asked, ‘Can a large quantity of water make a small quantity of what is unlawful as lawful?’
He (the Imam) then shook his hand like moving back something with the palm of his hand twice, saying, ‘No, no.’”
